outcomes.label: Died before maturity
outcomes.title: Established, then died of water stress before maturity (yield so far counted)

outcomes.label: Failed to establish
outcomes.title: Died before its canopy reached 5 %: a false start, the seedlings dried out

outcomes.label: Too late to mature
outcomes.title: Sown too late to reach maturity by 31 Mar, the season's end (counted as no yield)

outcomes.label: No sowing opportunity
outcomes.title: No onset by the rule's search end, 15 Jan (counted as no yield)

outcomes.label: Model error
outcomes.title: AquaCrop failed for this member: no outcome, left out of every probability

caveats: Experimental: maize is calibrated against trials at Kiboko (phenology and harvest index), sorghum only set against them; the crop forecasts have not been verified against observed crop outcomes.
Varieties are maturity classes (AquaCrop crop files with Kenyan plant densities), not calibrated cultivars.
Yields are water-limited: no nutrient stress, pests, diseases or management losses; they are an upper bound for smallholder fields.
Past seasons are simulated: AquaCrop grown in the observed weather of 1993–2025, not measured yields.
A crop season runs from 1 Aug to 31 Mar: a crop that cannot mature by 31 Mar is counted as too late.

After the last ERA5-Land day, temperature is the sub-seasonal model's own in its range (ECMWF extended range or GEFS runs, bias-corrected to ERA5-Land), then ECMWF SEAS5 member by member, bias-corrected to ERA5-Land, and ET0 the ERA5-Land climatology scaled by that temperature (Hargreaves); 1 Jan – 28 Feb rain is SEAS5 (bias-corrected), as for the Agri rules, and March rain SEAS5 quantile-mapped to CHIRPS. Where the SEAS5 files are missing, temperature is the 1993–2016 climatology and March rain the observed March of a past year (see each run's weather).
Soil is the 0.25° SoilGrids average of the site's grid cell, not a field measurement.
A second crop model, WOFOST 7.2, grows the same maize and sorghum members on the same dates; where the two disagree, the outlook depends on the model as much as on the weather.
Deterministic weather models are the same forecast in every member: their spread comes from SEAS5 only.
